drills.q: What is the exploration/exploitation tradeoff in one sentence?
drills.a: Choosing between trying options you're uncertain about to learn more (exploration) versus serving the currently best-known option to maximize immediate reward (exploitation).

drills.q: Why does a naive greedy bandit starve a brand-new content variant of traffic?
drills.a: The new variant starts with an uninformative/default reward estimate that's rarely competitive with an established variant's converged estimate, so a greedy policy never selects it -- a self-reinforcing loop where it's never explored because it looks unproven, and never stops looking unproven because it's never explored.

Select the action maximizing x^T theta_a_hat + alpha*sqrt(x^T A_a^-1 x): predicted reward (exploitation) plus an upper-confidence-bound exploration bonus that's large under high uncertainty and shrinks as data accumulates for that action in similar contexts.

drills.q: Compare Thompson Sampling and LinUCB -- when would you prefer each?
drills.a: Thompson Sampling samples from a full posterior per action, auto-balancing explore/exploit via posterior width with no tuning parameter -- good when you want a Bayesian model and automatic tuning. LinUCB uses an explicit tunable alpha for an auditable exploration knob -- good when stakeholders need to reason about exploration cost explicitly.

drills.q: Why does comparing 'personalized' against an arbitrary static baseline overstate personalization's value?
drills.a: The honest counterfactual is the best single non-personalized variant, not an arbitrary weak baseline. Comparing against a weak baseline credits personalization with gains that actually came from simply picking a better default, not from tailoring content per user/segment.

drills.q: Explain IPS off-policy evaluation and its main failure mode.
drills.a: Reweight logged rewards by (new policy's probability of the logged action / logging policy's probability of it), giving an estimate of the new policy's expected reward without live testing. Fails under support mismatch: if the new policy favors actions the logging policy rarely took, dividing by near-zero logging probabilities explodes the variance of the estimate.

drills.q: How do you check whether an OPE/IPS estimate should be trusted?
drills.a: Compute effective sample size (~1/mean(weights^2)); if far smaller than the raw logged sample, the estimate is dominated by a few extreme importance weights and shouldn't be trusted -- run a live experiment instead.

drills.q: Design a personalization strategy for a catalog where the top 5% of items get 80% of traffic and the rest is long-tail.
drills.a: Run a near-1:1 contextual bandit for the high-traffic head, where enough (context, action) data accumulates quickly to converge. For the long tail, use a hierarchical/segment-based model pooling across category or cluster so low-traffic items inherit a reasonable prior instead of running an under-powered individual bandit. Using the same 1:1 architecture uniformly would starve the long-tail majority of usable signal.

drills.q: A stakeholder wants to shut off all exploration once the bandit 'looks converged' to maximize short-term revenue. How do you respond?
drills.a: Push back: content and preference distributions drift over time, and zero ongoing exploration means the bandit silently ossifies around a policy that may no longer be optimal with no mechanism to detect the drift until performance visibly degrades. Propose a small bounded exploration floor instead of either extreme, framed as a quantifiable small cost to avoid a much larger invisible one.

drills.q: What's the connection between bandit cold start and hierarchical/partial-pooling Bayesian models?
drills.a: Same statistical idea in two systems: a new bandit action or a low-traffic Bayesian segment has no reliable individual signal, so both fixes borrow strength from a broader population (category/cluster/population prior), shrinking the individual estimate toward the shared one until enough own-data accumulates -- this can literally be implemented as a hierarchical Bayesian reward model inside the bandit.
